chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that they said:

Regarding the sacrificial animals of the People of the Book: 'If you witness them and they have mentioned the name of Allah, then eat their sacrifices; and if you do not witness them, do not eat; and if a Muslim man comes to you and informs you that they have mentioned [the name], then eat.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating the meat of the People of the Book according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the evidentiary standard for the permissibility of Ahl al-Kitab's meat, distinguishing between direct observation of the Basmala and reliance on the testimony of a trustworthy Muslim. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that uncertainty in the invocation requires verification, thereby safeguarding the ritual purity of consumption. This ruling underscores the importance of witness (*shuhud*) in establishing the legal validity of the slaughter act.
